business_problem: IBM’s CIO Organization needed to help new and early-tenure professionals manage IBM Z environments more independently because the mainframe skill curve was steep and subject matter experts were spending too much time answering routine questions, handling incidents, and guiding patching work.
solution_summary: IBM CIO deployed watsonx Assistant for Z as an on-premises generative AI and automation layer for mainframe operations. Running on an existing Red Hat OpenShift cluster, the assistant uses curated IBM Z knowledge and retrieval-augmented generation to answer product and operational questions, helping newer staff get digestible guidance without waiting for senior experts. The team also prioritized incident analysis and Db2 patching as early use cases: watsonx Assistant for Z can ingest incidents from a third-party workflow automation platform, suggest actions based on documentation and similar past events, and interact with Ansible-based automation plus change-management workflows to open, route, and close patching requests. This turns the assistant from a Q&A bot into an orchestration surface for routine mainframe operations. Because the CIO organization iterated with the product team during rollout, the deployment also improved the product itself while giving IBM a reusable pattern for bridging mainframe skills gaps with grounded AI plus operational automation.

data_flow: User questions and incidents enter watsonx Assistant for Z, RAG grounds responses in curated IBM Z content, incidents are enriched with historical and workflow-platform context, and the assistant can trigger Ansible-backed automations and change requests before reporting status back to the operations user.
business_outcome: The CIO Organization shortened onboarding, sped incident resolution and Db2 patching, and gave hundreds of users a more confident way to operate IBM Z without as much reliance on scarce experts.
